A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conformal hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) dielectric interface is of extreme importance for the improvement of carrier transport and heat dissipation in the two-dimensional (2D) material-based devices.

we use a plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD)-based process for the conformal growth of hexagonal-boron-nitride on SiO2 and Si substrates, with the purpose of improving the performance of WSe2-based field effect transistors.
we use plasma-enhanced CVD to grow 2D-BNs directly on 3D surfaces, and use it to improve the performance and thermal dissipations of WSe2 FETs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the atomically-clean conformal interface and better bridging of the vibrational spectrum of 2D-BNs across the interface can significantly improve thermal dissipation in a semiconductor device and thus the device performance.
the atomically-clean conformal interface and better interfacial heat transfer between 2D-BNs and substrates enable improved performance and thermal management in WSe2 transistors.
